summary: Rework of task 9.3 fixing the reproduced MEDIUM state-integrity defect SEC-9.3-01 and the SEC-9.3-02/03/04 hardening items. Atomicity: Plugin.UpdateConfiguration now validates the candidate BEFORE the base implementation persists anything (using the existing PluginConfigurationValidator, no duplicated logic), and the whole validate/persist/activate sequence is serialized with a per-plugin lock. An invalid candidate is rejected before persistence: the override does not call base.UpdateConfiguration at all, so a rejected candidate is never written to plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml, there is no crash window in which a rejected candidate is persisted, and there is no restore step for a concurrent valid save to overwrite. A valid candidate is persisted by base.UpdateConfiguration and activated by ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace. The previous TryRestoreLastValidConfiguration path was removed. This changes ADR-016 clause 4's ordering from 'base then TryReplace' to 'validate; if valid, base then TryReplace', so ADR-016 clause 4 was updated in place (per the rework instruction) and ADR-021 clause 5/consequences were updated to state that a rejected candidate is never persisted rather than restored. SEC-9.3-03: the IConfigurationRejectionNotifier interface documents the single-caller invariant (Plugin.TryNotifyRejected passes the validator's secret-free messages), and JellyfinConfigurationRejectionNotifier now sanitizes each reason (strips control characters, collapses whitespace runs, skips empty) in addition to the existing count cap (8) and 512/256 truncation. SEC-9.3-04: the notifier's bounded wait is injectable (second constructor) and a slow-CreateAsync containment test exercises the timeout branch in ~50ms. SEC-9.3-02: the activity-log volume/spam aspect is recorded in docs/limitations.md SEC-9. Docs overclaims about 'not left persisted' were corrected to the implemented validate-before-persist guarantee across ADR-016, ADR-021, architecture section 6, data-model 3.12, changelog, PLANS 9.3, project-status, and implementation-readiness. Preserved: never throws into the host (the plugin's validate/activate/notify logic is contained), no custom save route, valid save activates without restart, invalid save retains the last-valid public snapshot and private secrets, rejection surfaced via the activity-log entry. No task 9.4 work was implemented.

known_limitations: The rejected save's HTTP response remains 204 NoContent and the dashboard reports success; the rejection is surfaced only via the Activity log and, on reload, because the last valid configuration remains active and persisted (the rejected candidate was never written). Accepted per ADR-021.
Activity-log volume/spam (SEC-9.3-02): each rejected save writes one entry and consecutive-duplicate suppression is deliberately not implemented (ADR-021 clause 6); the trigger is administrator-only.

The activity-log write is best-effort (SEC-9.3-04): if IActivityManager is unavailable, CreateAsync throws, or it exceeds the bounded wait, no entry is written; the rejection and last-valid retention still hold and nothing is thrown.

base.UpdateConfiguration is not wrapped: a failure inside the host base method (for example an I/O failure in SaveConfiguration) propagates unchanged, as without the override. The plugin's validate/activate/notify logic itself never throws.

A valid candidate that cannot be activated because the running snapshot service is unavailable is persisted and is activated on the next host startup; the bounded secret-free validation result is still recorded.

Some singleton services capture OperationalLimits at construction (StateRepository cache/quota/retention; artwork artifact-size/decode limits); those values change only after a restart (pre-existing, outside the 9.3 acceptance criteria).
The bounded post-save reconciliation trigger (task 9.4) is not implemented.

Host-guarded tests (JellyfinHostFact) remain skipped because ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset (63 skips, identical to the pre-task baseline); the live pinned-host activity-log confirmation is owned by the live-verification task.
